hypotheses.title: AST build caches a facade for every syntax node/token on the long-lived SyntaxTree.RootNode, so the whole facade tree is retained for the entire compilation
hypotheses.issue: st/node.go:(*NonTerminalNodeBase).ChildInBucket lazily creates a facade (createFacade; e.g. (*STTokenBase).CreateFacade is ~144 B per token, non-terminal facades also allocate a childBuckets slice) for each accessed child and caches it in the parent's childBuckets forever. nodebuilder/mod.go:GetCompilationUnit / GetRecoveredCompilationUnit walk syntaxTree.RootNode, the root facade kept on st.SyntaxTree which the project holds for the whole compile. So every facade created during stage 2 (including the many keyword/punctuation tokens the builder only reads for kind/text/position: binary operators, return, ;, (, ), {, }, returns, function, ...) stays reachable until process exit. On a 20k-function file facade creation is ~61% of AST-build allocations (588 MB of 959 MB) and on corpus/bench/09-bench/huge-project-v 2.16 GB of 3.25 GB; none of it is ever freed. The retained heap raises peak RSS ~15-25% and increases GC scan work in every later stage (on large multi-module packages most of the wall-time cost shows up as GC during later stages).

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a token-heavy single-file Ballerina program whose runtime work is trivial.

usage: gen_repro.py <num_functions> <out.bal>
Each function has a handful of local declarations with binary expressions, so the
syntax tree has many tokens; main() calls only one function.
"""
import sys

n = int(sys.argv[1])
out = sys.argv[2]
lines = ["import ballerina/io;", ""]
for i in range(n):
    lines.append(f"function calc{i}(int input, int k) returns int {{")
    lines.append(f"    int a = input + {i} * k - 1;")
    lines.append("    int b = (a + k) * 2 - (input + 3);")
    lines.append("    int c = a + b + k + input + 4;")
    lines.append("    int d = c * 3 + b * 2 + a - k;")
    lines.append("    int e = d + c + b + a + 5;")
    lines.append("    return e - d + c - b + a;")
    lines.append("}")
    lines.append("")
lines.append("public function main() {")
lines.append(f"    io:println(calc{n - 1}(1, 2));")
lines.append("}")
with open(out, "w") as f:
    f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
reproducer.command: python3 gen_repro.py 20000 facade_20000.bal && go build -o /tmp/bal ./cli/cmd && /usr/bin/time -f 'wall %e s maxrss %M KB' /tmp/bal run --stats facade_20000.bal   (benchmark: ./bin/benchmark --mode memory|time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> facade_20000.bal)

hypotheses.baseline: facade_20000.bal on main: wall 8.96-9.53 s, max RSS 3.0-3.2 GB (benchmark mean 3028.9 MiB / 9531 ms). huge-project-v: 8.4-9.1 GB RSS, 38-58 s. 16-module x 4000-function package: 39-45 s, 9.2-9.9 GB.

hypotheses.fix_approach: The AST builder walks a private root facade instead of syntaxTree.RootNode: build a fresh unlinked ModulePart facade over syntaxTree.RootNode.InternalNode() (st.CreateUnlinkedFacade, as the parser does for RootNode) and SetSyntaxTree(syntaxTree) on it so FilePath/LineRange/TextDocument lookups still resolve. Positions are identical (root at position 0, child positions derived from internal widths), and diagnostics/IsMissing read shared internal nodes. Since ast/semantics don't keep st references, the private facade tree becomes garbage when the build returns. The facades on RootNode created earlier (e.g. projects/document_context.go:moduleLoadRequests reading imports) are kept as before, and no later consumer re-walks the tree after stage 2. Pitfall: simply clearing RootNode's childBuckets afterwards also works but would throw away cached facades and positions that other consumers (LS, import scanning) might rely on. Further gains possible: have the builder read token kind/text/width from internal nodes without creating token facades at all.

notes: Side observation (not pursued, close to an earlier capture-entry finding): deeply nested while loops scale cubically in stage 5 (depth 200/400/800 -> 0.2/0.97/8.7 s) because nested loop type resolvers walk the parent chain across capture entries.
